correctness.rationale: For independent components the bivariate conditional dynamic negative cumulative extropy reduces to Jλ(t)=1/2 ∫_0^t[1-(Fλ(x)/Fλ(t))²] dx with Fλ=1-exp(-λt). Differentiation gives Jλ'(t)=fλ(t)/Fλ(t)^3 ∫_0^t Fλ(x)^2 dx>0. Changing variables for Y_i=c_i X_i establishes exactly CJ_i^Y(t)=c_i CJ_i^X(t_i/c_i,t_j/c_j). For λ=ln2, J(1)=5/(4ln2)-3/2, J(2)=11/(12ln2)-7/9, hence 2J(1)-J(2)=(57-80ln2)/(36ln2)>0. The rigorous bound ln2<7/10<57/80 gives strict positivity. Direct symbolic and high-precision independent recomputation confirmed exact difference ~0.062044925852. Source Theorem 3.13 has the reverse inequality under these very hypotheses; discarding ψ' >=1 in its integral violates the required direction.

final_claim: Pandey--Kundu Theorem 3.13 CDNCEx dispersive-order implication is false: for independent X_i~Exp(log2), Y_i=2X_i meets the stated dispersive and monotonicity assumptions, but CJ_i^Y(2,2)-CJ_i^X(2,2)=(57-80log2)/(36log2)>0. General dilation scales each CDNCEx component by its corresponding coordinate factor.
limitations: Only Theorem 3.13 dispersive-order implication is disproved; no classification of additional sufficient conditions.
Bivariate independent exponential witness with dilation two; general scaling identity under positive constants.
